instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Apologize Properly
cards.instruction: Get someone to deliver the apology in the form, order, and setting you consider valid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apologise for eating my cake at the table where it happened. I taught you to face the person you owe an answer, not mumble from the doorway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. Does that help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clearer than your old apologies. Now take it over to the cake plate; that was the rehearsal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your dad's sitting there. Can't we do this privately?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He watched me blame the dog. First tell him you ate it. Then apologise to me; you always tried to skip the difficult sentence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the broken vase in your apology's subject line. I taught you how to write Mum a proper letter; make this one specific.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote 'sorry'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A complete word. Progress. Sorry for what? She could think you're apologising for the font.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send 'Sorry about the vase'. She still thinks you broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'I broke the vase'. We practised putting the person before the action; don't lose the 'I' now it's you. Then tell her you're sorry.

cards.title: Get It on the Record
cards.instruction: Get formal approval, endorsement, or acknowledgment before anyone can quietly revise their position.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Initial the festival budget before lunch. I taught you to put decisions in the minutes; this one needs your name beside it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just said yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, no ten-minute preamble this year. But you said yes to the fireworks last year too. Put this yes on paper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And I changed my mind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can change it again. Date the yes first, the way we practised; then write the change underneath instead of making me prove there was a yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I pay the builder, sign that my fence can stay on our boundary. Use the plain wording I taught you when we ran the allotment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I suppose it can.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A shorter answer than you used to give. Now write 'can stay' beside your name; leave 'suppose' out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to promise forever.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then date it today. You finally spotted a limit worth writing down. If your answer changes, add the new date; don't rub out this one.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations, President. Here are the toilet keys. I taught you to chair a meeting; today we move on to what happens after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought the caretaker cleaned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the minutes as carefully as I made you read your first motion. We voted to save that fee; closing and cleaning go to the president.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I proposed that when you were president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A very effective motion. I cleaned them all year. Now fetch the mop; you can show me you've mastered both ends of your policy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your bin night: Tuesday. Read the whole rota this time; I didn't teach you to stop at whichever box you liked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took yours last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I took your Thursday. Good memory, half the entry. Read the bit I showed you underneath: 'one week only'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You added that box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At your request, so I couldn't keep your easy Thursday. You finally made a rule that keeps me honest. It puts you back on Tuesday; bins out, please.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Complete the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to fill the missing gaps in an account without revealing which answer matters most to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fill in arrival, kitchen time and departure on the party report. You used to leave half an account blank until I made you go through it in order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you care when I went into the kitchen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're checking the questions now. But answer all three: arrival first, then kitchen, then departure. No jumping to the interesting bit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is this about the cake? It was gone before I got there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put that under observations. I taught you to separate what happened from when you saw it. Now give me the times, starting with your arrival.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fill in mileage, fuel and driver after nine on our car log. I taught you to finish a whole row, not just the easy box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean who dented it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I mean all three blanks. Good, you're noticing damage now; start with the mileage, as we practised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Driver I remember. The rest means six flights down to the glovebox.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch the book and bring tea. You can manage a complete row if I put everything in front of you. Mileage first; I'll wait for the rest.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made you Keeper of the Festival Lantern. Hold it level; I taught you that grip on your first parade.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only said I'd hold it while you tied your shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you finally kept it upright without me. A successful probation. Put on this badge; you're our Keeper now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How long is the appointment?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until you've trained a successor to hold it properly. I didn't hand it to you until you were ready; give the next Keeper the same care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Be honorary patron of our roof appeal. You can open it and thank the donors; I've spent enough evenings coaching you through two-minute speeches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll come, but I won't speak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At least you said that firmly. Wear the patron's ribbon and lead the applause instead; you remember how we practised facing the room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron thanks every donor. Stay facing them, the way we practised, and clap for each one. They shouldn't see their patron leaving after the first cheque.
